settings.label: Enemy Highlight Color

default.note: The option label itself reads 'Red (Default)' in third-party captures.

settings.verificationNotes: Setting name confirmed by Riot (Patch 12.06 bug fix mentions the Enemy Highlight Color setting set to red). Option labels and the Accessibility location come from third-party guides.
settings.description: Sets the color used to outline and highlight enemies. The options are labelled for color vision deficiencies, but anyone can choose the color they see best.
settings.tradeoffs: Which color stands out depends on the person's color vision and the map, so only the player can judge this.

settings.label: Sensitivity: Aim
settings.verificationNotes: Label and range not confirmed by a current Riot source; the slider bounds are prototype validation bounds, not the game's verified range.
settings.description: Mouse sensitivity for aiming.
settings.tradeoffs: Personal aim preference. VALORANT and CS2 use different sensitivity scales, so the assistant never proposes or transfers a number.

settings.label: Scoped Sensitivity Multiplier
settings.verificationNotes: Label and range not confirmed by a current Riot source; the bounds are prototype validation bounds.
settings.description: Multiplier applied to aim sensitivity while scoped.
settings.tradeoffs: Personal aim preference; the assistant never proposes a number.

settings.label: Rotate
settings.description: Whether the minimap rotates with the direction you face or stays in a fixed orientation.
settings.tradeoffs: A rotating map matches your view; a fixed map keeps callout positions in the same place on screen.

settings.label: Fixed Orientation

availability.note: Greyed out unless Rotate is set to Fixed (as in Riot's screenshot).

settings.description: When the minimap is fixed, whether it always uses the same orientation or flips based on your side (attack/defense).

settings.label: Keep Player Centered
settings.description: Keeps your position at the center of the minimap instead of showing the whole map region.

settings.label: Minimap Size
settings.verificationNotes: Label and a value of 1.1 visible in Riot's screenshot; the slider range is not documented, so bounds are prototype values.
settings.description: Size of the minimap on the HUD.

settings.label: Minimap Zoom
settings.verificationNotes: Label and a value of 0.9 visible in Riot's screenshot; the slider range is not documented, so bounds are prototype values.
settings.description: How much of the map the minimap shows; lower values show more of the map.

settings.label: Minimap Vision Cones
settings.description: Shows the direction your teammates are looking as cones on the minimap.

hints.why: Vision cones show which angles teammates are already watching.

settings.label: Show Map Region Names
settings.description: Controls when region names appear on the large map (opened with M). It only affects that map, not the minimap in your HUD.
settings.tradeoffs: Region names help learn callouts but add text on the map.

settings.label: First Person Handedness
settings.description: Shows your first-person weapon on the left or right side of the screen.

settings.label: Always Show Inventory
settings.description: Keeps your weapon and ability inventory visible on the HUD.

settings.label: Player Loadouts Always Visible
settings.description: On shows loadout boxes above allies' heads; Off hides them.
settings.tradeoffs: More information above teammates, but more on-screen clutter.

settings.label: Cycle to Next/Prev Weapon Wraps Inventory
settings.description: Whether cycling to the next or previous weapon wraps around from the last slot to the first.

settings.label: Show Bullet Tracers
settings.description: Shows bullet tracer effects.

settings.label: Show Spectator Count
settings.description: Shows how many players are spectating you.

hints.why: Hides one non-essential HUD element.

settings.label: Use Team Color for Crosshair Color
settings.description: Uses your team color as the crosshair color.

settings.label: Hide User Interface In Game
settings.description: Set to On to hide your HUD.
settings.tradeoffs: Hides information you normally need during play; mostly useful for capturing footage.

settings.label: Hide First Person Arms (Observers Only)
settings.description: For observers: hides the first-person arms of the spectated player.

settings.label: Show Full Screen Blind for Observers
settings.description: For observers: shows the full-screen blind effect when the spectated player is flashed.

settings.label: Team Colors Affect HUD for Observers
settings.description: For observers: tints the HUD with team colors.

settings.label: Explicit Language Filter
settings.description: Filters explicit language in chat.

settings.label: Show Blood
settings.description: Shows blood effects when players are hit.
settings.tradeoffs: Blood is also a visual confirmation that a shot landed.

hints.why: Removes one visual effect from the screen; note that blood also confirms hits.

settings.label: Show Corpses
settings.description: Shows the bodies of eliminated players.

settings.label: Show Mature Content
settings.description: Shows mature content during gameplay.

settings.label: Network Buffering
settings.description: How much incoming network data is buffered before it is shown. More buffering smooths over unstable connections.
settings.tradeoffs: More buffering can smooth packet loss or jitter but adds a small delay before you see updates.

hints.why: Extra buffering can smooth out an unstable connection.
Less buffering means less added delay before updates appear.

settings.label: Instability Indicators
settings.description: Shows indicators when network or performance problems are detected.

hints.why: Lets you see when a problem comes from the network rather than your settings.

settings.label: Show Teammate Loadouts (Hold)

default.note: Left Alt shown in Riot's screenshot.

settings.description: Hold to show teammates' loadouts.

settings.label: Toggle Menus
settings.description: Opens and closes menus.

settings.label: Combat Report
settings.description: Shows or hides the combat report that pops up when you die.

settings.label: Agent Ability Tooltip
settings.description: Shows your Agent's ability descriptions.

settings.label: Open Armory
settings.description: Opens the buy menu.

settings.label: Open Map (Toggle)
settings.description: Toggles the large map.

settings.label: Open Map (Hold)

default.note: Caps Lock shown in Riot's screenshot.

settings.description: Shows the large map while held.

settings.label: Show Scoreboard (Hold)
settings.description: Shows the scoreboard while held.

settings.label: Toggle Cursor

default.note: Middle Mouse Button shown in Riot's screenshot.

settings.description: Shows the mouse cursor in game.

settings.label: Replay Bookmarking

default.note: Riot: blank by default on PC.

settings.verificationNotes: Riot gives the path Settings > Controls > Interface > Replay Bookmarking (Patch 13.10); the section inside Interface is not stated.
settings.description: Bookmarks the current moment for later review in Replays (added in Patch 13.10).

tabs.label: Crosshair
tabs.note: Not simulated: no current (2026) Riot source documents the crosshair editor's exact labels and value ranges. See docs/GAME_SETTINGS_AUDIT.md.

settings.label: Display Mode
settings.verificationNotes: Riot confirms a Fullscreen display mode under Video > General (Oct 2026). The other option labels come from secondary sources.
settings.description: Chooses how the game window is presented. Riot suggests testing Fullscreen, which may improve performance on some systems by keeping the game focused on the display.
settings.tradeoffs: Fullscreen can make switching to other windows slower; the performance effect varies by system.

hints.why: Riot says Fullscreen may improve performance on some systems by keeping the game focused on the display.

settings.label: Resolution
settings.verificationNotes: Options depend on the display; this list is simulated for a 1920x1080 display.
settings.description: Sets the rendering resolution.

settings.label: Aspect Ratio Method
settings.description: When the resolution's shape differs from the display, Letterbox adds bars while Fill stretches the image.

settings.label: Limit FPS Always
settings.description: Caps the frame rate at all times. Riot suggests a cap to keep your PC from working too hard, set lower than the average FPS you get while playing.
settings.tradeoffs: A cap reduces heat and load but limits the maximum frame rate.
settings.verificationNotes: The numeric cap that accompanies this toggle is not simulated because its exact label and range are not documented.

settings.label: Limit FPS in Background
settings.description: Throttles the frame rate while the game is in the background.

settings.label: NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency
settings.verificationNotes: Riot has not published the option names; labels and the Video > General location come from secondary sources.
settings.description: NVIDIA's low-latency mode, which aims to reduce system latency. 'On + Boost' trades extra GPU power for lower latency.
settings.tradeoffs: Boost may increase GPU power use; the latency benefit depends on whether the GPU is the bottleneck.

hints.why: Reflex is designed to reduce system latency, most noticeably when the GPU is the bottleneck.

settings.label: Multithreaded Rendering
settings.description: Can improve CPU performance and graphics quality on high spec devices. Riot lists minimum specs: 8 GB RAM, 2 GB VRAM and a CPU with at least 8 cores (physical and virtual).
settings.tradeoffs: Riot suggests turning it off when troubleshooting crashes; benefits depend on meeting the minimum specs.

hints.why: Riot says it can improve CPU performance on high-spec devices (8 GB RAM, 2 GB VRAM, 8+ cores).

settings.label: Material Quality
settings.description: Quality of surface materials. Riot names it among the most useful settings to adjust when trying to improve performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Lower settings reduce visual detail; Riot advises lowering gradually and testing after each change.

hints.why: Riot lists Material Quality among the most useful settings to adjust for performance; lower it one step at a time and test.
Higher material quality preserves surface detail.

settings.label: Texture Quality
settings.description: Resolution of textures. Riot names it among the most useful settings to adjust when trying to improve performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Lower settings make surfaces blurrier; Riot advises lowering gradually and testing.

hints.why: Riot lists Texture Quality among the most useful settings to adjust for performance; lower it one step at a time and test.
Higher texture quality keeps surfaces sharp.

settings.label: Detail Quality
settings.description: Amount of environmental detail. Riot names it among the most useful settings to adjust when trying to improve performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Lower settings remove some environmental detail; Riot advises lowering gradually and testing.

hints.why: Riot lists Detail Quality among the most useful settings to adjust for performance; lower it one step at a time and test.
Higher detail quality keeps environmental detail.

settings.label: UI Quality
settings.description: Quality of interface rendering. Riot names it among the most useful settings to adjust when trying to improve performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Lower settings can make interface elements look less crisp.

hints.why: Riot lists UI Quality among the most useful settings to adjust for performance.

settings.label: Vignette
settings.description: Darkens the edges of the screen as a stylistic effect.

hints.why: Riot's troubleshooting guide lists Vignette: Off when minimizing video effects.
Without the vignette the screen edges are not darkened.

settings.label: VSync
settings.description: Synchronizes the game's frame rate with your monitor to help prevent screen tearing. Disabling it may improve performance or reduce input delay in some cases, but it can cause visible tearing.
settings.tradeoffs: Riot: if you test with VSync disabled, turn it back on if the tearing is more noticeable than any performance improvement.

hints.why: Riot says disabling VSync may reduce input delay in some cases, at the cost of possible screen tearing.
Riot says disabling VSync may improve performance in some cases.
Riot says VSync can help prevent screen tearing.

settings.label: Anti-Aliasing
settings.verificationNotes: Riot confirms the setting (written 'Anti Aliasing' in the May 2026 crash guide). Option labels come from a Sept 2026 third-party guide; any further options (e.g. FXAA) are not confirmed and are not simulated.
settings.description: Smooths jagged edges. Riot's general guidance lists anti-aliasing among the settings with a large performance impact.
settings.tradeoffs: Lower anti-aliasing shows more jagged edges.

hints.why: Riot lists anti-aliasing among the settings that most affect performance in its general guidance.
More anti-aliasing smooths edges.

settings.label: Anisotropic Filtering
settings.verificationNotes: Riot confirms the label and the 1x value; the 2x-16x steps are corroborated by a third-party guide.
settings.description: Keeps textures sharp when viewed at steep angles.
settings.tradeoffs: Lower filtering makes distant floors and walls blurrier.

hints.why: Riot's troubleshooting guide uses 1x as the lowest-cost setting; stepping down reduces texture filtering work.

settings.label: Improve Clarity
settings.verificationNotes: Riot's May 2026 crash guide writes 'Improve Quality'; the newer Oct 2026 guide's 'Improve Clarity' is used.
settings.description: An image clarity enhancement. Riot lists it among the additional visual effects you can try disabling to improve performance.

hints.why: Riot lists Improve Clarity among visual effects to try disabling for performance.

settings.label: Experimental Sharpening
settings.description: An experimental image sharpening filter. Riot lists it among the additional visual effects you can try disabling to improve performance.

hints.why: Riot lists Experimental Sharpening among visual effects to try disabling for performance.

settings.label: Bloom
settings.description: Adds a glow around bright light sources. Riot lists it among the additional visual effects you can try disabling to improve performance.

hints.why: Riot lists Bloom among visual effects to try disabling for performance.
Bloom is part of the game's intended lighting look.

settings.label: Distortion
settings.description: Screen distortion effects from some abilities and explosions. Riot lists it among the additional visual effects you can try disabling to improve performance.

hints.why: Riot lists Distortion among visual effects to try disabling for performance.
Fewer warping effects over the scene.

settings.label: Cast Shadows
settings.verificationNotes: Riot's May 2026 crash guide lists 'First Person Shadows'; the newer Oct 2026 guide's 'Cast Shadows' is used.
settings.description: Renders dynamic shadows. Riot lists it among the additional visual effects you can try disabling to improve performance.

hints.why: Riot lists Cast Shadows among visual effects to try disabling for performance.

settings.label: AMD Anti-Lag 2

availability.note: Requires compatible AMD hardware with drivers from March 9th, 2026 or later (Riot, Patch 12.09).

settings.verificationNotes: Support added in Patch 12.09 (official). Riot's notes give no menu label or location; the label and bottom-of-Graphics-Quality placement come from a third-party guide.
settings.description: AMD Anti-Lag 2 reduces input latency in certain GPU-bound scenarios.

hints.why: Riot says Anti-Lag 2 reduces input latency in certain GPU-bound scenarios.

subtabs.label: Stats
subtabs.note: Stat display options are not simulated (labels not confirmed since the 12.07 revamp).

settings.label: Overall Volume
settings.description: Master volume for all game audio.

settings.label: Sound Effects Volume
settings.description: Volume of gameplay sound effects such as footsteps, gunfire and abilities.

settings.label: Voice-over Volume
settings.description: Volume of Agent and announcer voice lines.

settings.label: All Music Overall Volume
settings.description: Overall volume of all game music.

settings.label: Enable HRTF
settings.description: Head-related transfer function audio processing, which simulates 3D sound direction on headphones.
settings.tradeoffs: Designed for headphones; how natural it sounds varies by person.

hints.why: HRTF processing can make the direction of sounds easier to place on headphones.

settings.label: VOIP Ducks Music
settings.description: Lowers music volume while voice chat is active.

hints.why: Lowering music while teammates speak makes callouts easier to hear.

settings.label: Output Device

default.note: 'Default System Device' shown in Riot's screenshot.

settings.description: Audio device used for voice chat output.

settings.label: Input Device

default.note: 'Default System Device' shown in Riot's screenshot.

settings.description: Microphone used for voice chat.

settings.label: Incoming Volume
settings.verificationNotes: Label confirmed by Riot's screenshot, which shows no numeric scale; 0-100% is a prototype scale.
settings.description: Volume of other players' voices.

settings.label: Mic Volume
settings.verificationNotes: Label confirmed by Riot's screenshot, which shows no numeric scale; 0-100% is a prototype scale.
settings.description: Input gain of your microphone.

settings.label: Loopback Test
settings.description: Plays your microphone back to you. If you can hear your voice in this test, your device settings are fine.

settings.label: Mic Sensitivity Threshold
settings.verificationNotes: Label confirmed by Riot's screenshot, which shows no numeric scale; 0-100% is a prototype scale.
settings.description: How loud input must be before the microphone transmits when using automatic activation.

settings.label: Party Voice Chat
settings.description: Voice chat with your party (players you started matchmaking with).

hints.why: Needed to talk with your party.

settings.label: Party Voice During Custom Game
settings.description: Keeps party voice chat active in custom games.

settings.label: Party Voice Activation Mode
settings.description: Push-to-talk requires holding a key (U by default) to be heard; Automatic transmits when your voice is detected.

settings.label: Team Voice Chat
settings.description: Voice chat with your whole team. Team voice chat is push-to-talk only; V is the default keybind.

hints.why: Needed to hear and give team callouts.
